attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his own Substack post, rebutting a critic's objection. He endorses them.

semantics.note: An unhedged present-tense factual rebuttal: quick Google Images searches turn up many people drawing left-handed, so the critic's no-training-data objection is wrong. The scope limit to one critic's objection is kept.

contract.note: The plain reading of 'a few seconds' and 'lots' is ordinary. Requiring training-exposure evidence goes slightly beyond his words, since he cited only public availability. That could matter later, but it does not decide this case because no outcome evidence was retrieved.

reviews.rationale: The packet has no usable evidence items. Every source considered was unused: some were unreadable, undated, or returned 404/403 errors. There is no dated Google Images capture or reconstruction for 2024-02-13, and no readable training record for the system. The reviewer found no counterevidence either. The available evidence does not settle the claim.
